verdict.for_whom: Suits action game fans once technical issues settle. Worth knowing: it requires an always-online connection, and performance includes crashes and freezing early on.

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial reviews show severe technical complaints and negative sentiment during the opening window, while players with more time report positive experiences despite ongoing performance flaws.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players encounter immediate technical barriers, including launch crashes, cutscene freezes, input responsiveness issues, and mandatory background software alongside an always-online connection.

Its unfortunate, I wanted to give this game a try since it looked like fun but not only does it take over 10 mins to load, when I finally get in the game it freezes and crashes when loading cutscenes.... just no... I'm refunding this.

claims.claim: Reviewers complain about forced data collection and intrusive background software installed with the game.

citations.review_text: This game has an absurd data collection policy that you cannot opt out of regardless of where you live. Pretty game, but have more respect for yourself than to buy something that disrespects you with data harvesting and a live service model that doesn't belong in what is normally a $60 purchase.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as messy and note that the game sometimes ignores inputs.

citations.review_text:
I like this game but honestly, the controls are an absolute mess. For something as simple as an horde shooter to feel this messy I wouldnt recommand it. 
Especialy when you have a key bind to switch ranged weapons but mouse 1 and mouse 2 are both melee and ranged. Not to forget the game sometimes feels like it just ignores your inputs in general.

Only buy in HEAVY discount. 

The game controls are annoying. In the previous Space Marine title you had a separate button for melee attack modifier. Now you have the same button that does the regular attacks also do the special/stun attack, but it feels there is some arbitrary hold duration. So I can't ever know which attack I am charging a series/combo power attack or which I am going for a stun attack. The stupid consolified controls and UI are just a mess. 

The game scenery - the first 5 minutes you are met with not great attention to detail. They could have put more effort into polishing animations. The first big scene you see - you LITERALLY see the entities popping in out. They could have at least hidden the bugs and soldiers to have appear and dissapear behind some vision blockers. 

The character takes too much space and there is no option to edit the camera position. You are basically having a 4:3 usable screen space. Mouse movement also feels weird. Also weird scaling between aimed mode and regular viewing mode. No option for aimed sensitivity and regular sensitivity. 

Adding to that the ♥♥♥♥ that is being isntalled along with the game makes this whole thing very icky. 

And considering Saber is involved - no wonder. Seeing how they did Quake Champions it is no surprise how this ended up. The moment I saw the trailers of items moving in space with misaligned movement and direction, as well as the lighting, I guessed Saber is involved without even researching into it. The Swarm Engine is basically Saber3D that was used for Quake Champions and which crashed it to the ground. So again no warm feelings for Saber. 

Really not impressed and not for this kind of money. I really HATE how modern game development is just doing consoles first and BARELY any effort for the PC port and its controlls. And Saber is involved, so more minus points. 

TLDR: This is yet another money grab console port that is primarily a platform for DLC sale with something like a simpli…

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players experience a linear campaign with animation-locked melee combat and performance instability, alongside cosmetic DLC paywalls.

claims.claim: The campaign takes around eight to twelve hours to complete.

citations.review_text: gameplay is awesome, but i am disappointed about campaign, a game with so much lore you offer an 8 hours straight of campaign which i was expecting for at least 50 hours of campaign gameplay. such a shame

As someone who has played the game since it has dropped on PS and moving to PC recently, I've really had no reason to continue the game after completing the campaign. All the PVP and PVE modes are very repetitive, similar to the D2 strike missions, and most of the rewards feel like a drag to collect just to unlock lame cosmetics while all the cool stuff is locked behind a $5.00 "DLC" pack that's really just an armor pack. It's crazy how they'll still have you pay full price for the game and then spam microtransactions if you want to look anything different from the base space marine, but what else should I have expected from a game made from Games Workslop. For those who are considering purchasing the game understand that for $60 at full price you are getting an 8 hour (roughly) campaign and a grinding simulator game that's very repetitive and all the unique space marine chapter items will be locked behind a paywall. Genuinely have seen Roblox games that have outperformed this one in terms of PVP battling.

This was a tough yes decision for me.

Yes, the game looks and sounds very good. Especially Tyranid hordes, environments, the feel on hub between missions. Requires some hardware to run though, especially with good graphics.

No, the multiplayer component is clearly meant to be majority of the game and the time sink. I'm not interested so I had to manually turn off Internet from Windows to go around the always online requirement and all the data collection and what-not trash.

Maybe, the story is suprisingly short. Was it 5 mission... maybe six? 12 hours and it's through. Could have been easily below 10 with more efficient time usage I suppose. While the story was just okay in general, It had very nice elements and nicely continued Titus' story.

Maybe, the gameplay is kinda nice. Fights look and feel nice, and it started good. But at least normal difficulty, you can soon learn the strategy. Just forget the everyday mob (except random counters for their attacks) and just go for bigger ones. Tyranid warriors and Chaos space marines. When they die, mob around them also dies. And weaponry... ugh, it's so poor. You have melta weapons (which are the best I think as you're constantly in melee and execution moves), lascannon, plasmagun, heavy bolter and dozen or so different bolter guns. I know Marines weaponry isn't most varied, but sheez it was boring to choose from 4 different, yet nearly identical bolter guns.

Overall, if you are fan of warhammer and / or multiplayer enthusiastic, then sure, go for it. Otherwise, wait for a sale like I did.

Personally, I just couldn't care less about warhammers golden boys, space marines and their evil edgy counterpars chaos marines. I think they are so boring. Where are eldar? Tau? Maybe Necrons? I did like Tyranids in this game very much though.

It's a fun game for a couple of hours. 

The single player was fun and only took around 8hours to complete. I then tried some "multiplayer" with bots and it was a awful experience. All the enemies gang up on you alone and the teammates were dumber then rocks.  Still it's a multiplayer mode so I guess it's my fault for trying it with bots.

claims.claim: The campaign levels are linear corridors.

citations.review_text:
I am new to the W40k universe, so with that in mind...

THE GOOD
Visuals
Gory finishers
Lore and story - as far as I can tell
Multiple game modes to enjoy - Campaign, PvE missions, challenges, PVP
Enjoyable co-op

THE WEIRD
The game didn't wanna run at stable 1080p 60 fps on my rig in large empty interiors but ran 60 stable with hundreds of enemies on the screen so I had to use DLSS+framegen to make it smooth.
Early mission sections sometimes transport you into a new place without an obvious transition.

THE BAD
85% of the levels are just S-shaped corridors going into another S-shaped corridor, which can be hard to navigate especially in the jungle or the factory setting, since every building in this universe is so large.
The small rat-sized enemies are super clunky
The menus can be pretty slow since the game is made to allow a quick drop-in and drop-out of other players.

SUMMARY
SM2 is a great action game, a must-have if you enjoy the universe or want a new co-op game to grind through with up to 2 of your friends.

If you just want to enjoy all of the meat solo like myself, it can be somewhat lacking so consider getting it on a discount and see if you like it. 

I have enjoyed it a lot, I just wish there was more unique stuff to explore and fight.

Game is  nice, shooting feals amazing,
recomend playing with controller and the story is interesting, 

how ever the price is way to high for such a short game at slow pace and looking aroundthe levels i finishedthe game in 11 hours. 

Even if the levels are really polished and handcrafted and filled with detail it is really lenear. 

Recommend on DEEP SALE ONLY!

citations.review_text: Do you enjoy being animation locked every 5 secs? Compared to Darktide, Vermintide or even Gears of War the melee combat in this game is truly bad and the number 1 reason why people don't play. All other games have freedom of movement , it's not fun to be locked , truly disappointing. Can't even jump. No bullet decals ,some objects don't even register phsical hits.

A lot of people like the game, thats cool a lot of people like to smoke crack and groom kids too that doesnt make it good. Combat just sucks, it wants to demand you get good at it but it doesnt have the decency to be fun enough to want to. Your sword has no weight, your gun shoots BB's and your character feels like hes moving under water. Animation locks galore as you swing your cardboard sword and dozens of enemies chip away at you with guns from across the screen while youre stuck perma dodging the 40 zerglings that threaten to evaporate your whole health bar should you stop dodge roll spamming. Its a spectacle and WH is a cool universe but the execution here is bad. Some people, mega fans of WH might like it but theres a reason this game lives on a deep discount to barely maintain its tiny player base. Most people will not enjoy horde shooter dark souls aka SM II

claims.claim: Reviewers experience persistent server disconnections during multiplayer operations that result in lost progress and experience.

citations.review_text:
Game keeps disconnecting from servers on multiplayer, I have tried all fixes that I could find to no avail.
there are better days when I am getting maybe one or two and there are others when it is impossible to play a match in full.
Game itself is engaging, fun to play and learning curve is steep but rewarding, I wish story (single player) was a bit longer. 
there is also a bit too much loading screens for my taste.
All in all if disconnection issues are solved this will be really good game, but for now it is a bit disappointing to play and be disconnected near the end of operation etc.

The missions are too long and at least once a play session, I get disconnected in the middle of the mission or near the end even and all the experience and credits I would earn are completely lost due to no fault of mine. claims.claim: Reviewers describe launch stability issues, citing crashes and extended troubleshooting required to start the game.

citations.review_text: You have to spend 30-60 minutes every time you want to play to figure out 5 different reasons why it keeps crashing on laucnh this time. I spent more time reading forum posts than playing the game. Once it launches its fine. I dont know if its the easy anti cheat or what, but this should not be acceptible for a 2 year old game in 2026, especially since MANY people seem to have the same issue and is nowhere adressed by the company it seems.

Holy moly moly holy, I absolutely loved this game, and have found only 2 issues with it in my whole time playing. So, I had wanted to buy this game for a long time, and had no idea that I would get so incredibly hooked. The gameplay loop is insanely satisfying, taking on hordes of enemies hundreds and thousands at a time is incredible. The story is adrenaline pumped directly into the veins, with the most testosterone fueled ending mission i've ever played. Customisation and operation missions that run concurrently with the main campaign is where I sunk most of my hours, and I have no regrets. If you love horde fighting games and large scale battle games, buy this immediately when on sale. Now for the issues, two fairly significant ones. Firstly, the PVP modes are some of the worst things i've ever seen, with insanely imbalanced skill levels amongst matchmaking, the slowest servers of all time, mostly due to no interest at all in those servers, and essentially what can be decribed as grenade spam and overstimulation, which is a crazy statement considering the amount of particle affects that occur during the main story. Another issue is the Alt+tab phenomenon, which only occurred in my last 10-12 hours of playtime, which is perhaps the most infuriating thing of all time. You will tab out, the game freezes, and then crashes. It is genuinely a major issue that is WELL KNOWN, so to fix it I recommend turning off Hardware accelerated Gpu Scheduling. ANYWHO, amazing game that is easily in my top five, just with a couple of issues that aren't even central to the game and shouldn't occur for most players, would definitely recommend to those players I previously mentioned. BUY IT FOR THE EMPEROR OR DIE!

Overall, great game and a must get when on sale for any Warhammer 40k fans. :D

there are better days when I am getting maybe one or two and there are others when it is impossible to play a match in full.
Game itself is engaging, fun to play and learning curve is steep but rewarding, I wish story (single player) was a bit longer.

TL:DR: The game is a great brawler/shooter that really gives you the feeling that you're a space marine.
-
The combat feels great, the music is awesome, the campaign is impactful even if it's a tad short, the PvE is excellent, and there's even PvP.

Excellent game for the price, even better on sale, and the in-game purchases are all cosmetics (with plenty of things you can unlock for absolutely free).

Speaking of unlocks, they are well paced and the armor pieces are all well crafted (even though there are a few that are quite bland but more variety is good).

The weapons all feel different and each one has a slot to fill on the battlefield. The different classes have weapons that multiple can use which makes leveling other classes easier with a better weapon.
-
To the point, the game is fun and an excellent way to play around as a space marine in the 40k setting.
Titus is the GOAT.
-
FOR THE EMPEROR!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the parry and dodge systems as strict, requiring precise timing and learning distinct combat cues.

citations.review_text:
Massively overrated with some of the most inconsistent, contradictory, frustrating game design I've ever experienced. 

The audio-visual design is trash and makes combat an absolutely unreadable cluster, with multiple systems competing for your attention (dodge and parry cues sharing the same audio indicator is a particularly egregious sin); the gameplay tries to chase that "deliberate and measured" trend from "soulslike" games combined with character-action horde combat, which just results in a clunky game where you're easily overwhelmed; game mechanics are littered with exceptions and inconsistencies, particularly with enemy attacks and the parry system; the control schemes available are all generally awkward and awful no matter which of the limited options you pick (none of them do a good job combining both melee and gun combat while allowing easy use of abilities, there's always a trade-off); the general UI is convoluted, makes party management awkward and needlessly hides various screens; pointless loading screens that shouldn't exist (I shouldn't have to reload the hangar when leaving a party!); an upgrade system that is often confusing and somewhat of a slog; the list goes on and on and on.....

I tried to like it, I really did, but in the end the experience keeps pissing me off. Makes Darktide look competent by comparison, which is saying a lot.

Came in expecting the gameplay to be like helldivers, got very pleasantly surprised. 
Definitely one of the best games i've played lately 100% recommend if you love satisfying perfect parries and perfect dodges. Graphics are extremely good and the game runs really well. In addition to great visuals and insanely satisfying gameplay that forces you to keep alternating between offensive and defensive playstyles, the sound design is immaculate. 10/10 would recommend.

Loving the coop gameplay and difficulty variation you're able to do with players and how populated each difficulty is with coop. Will go ahead and let anyone who is going to play, the parry and blocking aspect of the game is not forgivable at all and i recommend watching a couple tutorials and also experimenting with it before thinking you know what each one means. they don't mean what you think they mean. Overall the game has been super fun, interesting and takes alot of time to progress everything so its not a 10hour game and youre maxxed out which i love about it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as demanding strict timing for parries and dodges, functioning similarly to a souls-like game where improper execution leads to being quickly defeated.

citations.review_text:
I had no history on anything Warhammer related going into this and just thought it'd be like Vermintide 2, which I liked. BOY WAS I IN FOR A TREAT.. This game is simply FANTASTIC! The movement, combat and ESPEICALLY the world building is so well thought out and implemented. Not only that but the combat is extremely challenging on harder difficulties and is pretty much like a souls-like game where you have to know your combos or else you'll get downed. 
Other great highlights include the extremely detailed armor customization and being able to adjust both your perks and weapon upgrades for exactly the type of playstyle you like. I also cannot believe how stable this game is online, from all the times that I've been playing co-op or in random match-making lobbies has the game crashed once in the 40 hours I have currently put in. 
Yeah, great game!

Characters and dialogue are excellent.

Gameplay is super fun. Both PvP & PvE. 

It's an incredible peak fantasy game. Full-on action-packed fantasy.

Love it. 

A solid 9/10 game to me.

FOR THE EMPEROR!

Incredible introduction to 40k. I had no idea what I was getting myself into, and now I'm all in. The combat is like no other. Countless finishers that vary based on your class, weapons, and the enemy you're slaying. This gives the game an added layer of replayability. 

The community is great. The PvP is buggy, however it's primarily a PvE game. Despite its flaws, the PvP is a beautiful throwback to a much simpler and enjoyable 360 era, and it still gets a lot right. With the regular updates (all playable content is included with the base game), I can see myself putting A LOT more hours into this. 

Victorus aut Mortis!
